# Using Maestro in Cursor / Cursor CLI

<!-- Generated by `node packages/cli build` from the harness registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

The skill is the same in every agent. This guide covers only what is specific to Cursor / Cursor CLI.

## Install

Project scope (one repository): copy this skill folder to `.cursor/skills/maestro/`.

User scope (every project): copy it to `~/.cursor/skills/maestro/`.

From the gti-skills repository, the CLI does the copy for you:

```bash
node packages/cli install --harness cursor --skill maestro
node packages/cli install --harness cursor --skill maestro --scope user
```

Restart the agent session after installing so it rescans its skills.

## Use

Describe the task in plain language. Cursor / Cursor CLI loads the skill when the request matches its `description`. You can also run it explicitly by typing `/maestro`.

## Where the skill finds its files

`<skill-dir>` in `SKILL.md` is the folder that contains `SKILL.md`: `.cursor/skills/maestro` for a project install, or `~/.cursor/skills/maestro` for a user install. Scripts and references are always addressed relative to it.

## Verify

Ask the agent which skills it has loaded and check that `maestro` is listed.

## Notes

- Cursor CLI reads the same folders. Cursor also loads .agents/skills, .claude/skills, and .codex/skills.
- Maestro delegates every step. Load the model preferences and the provider catalog before choosing a worker, read references/harness/adapters.md before the first spawn, and record the worker chat id before the first prompt.
- Cursor can return a resumable chat id from its subagent tool and the Cursor CLI resumes with --resume; use whichever path gives a chat id you can prompt again.
- Documentation: [Cursor / Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/docs/skills) (path source: official).
